THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner is sought to be prosecuted for the offenses punishable under Sections 406, 417, 420,
and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
The prosecution's case alleges that the defacto complainant and accused No.1 were in a relationship, and their marriage was solemnized in 2003.
Prior to the marriage, accused No.2, the mother of accused No.1, insisted that the defacto complainant purchase a site jointly with accused No.1 for security.
Accordingly, the defacto complainant bought a site jointly in his and accused No.1's name.
After the marriage, due to incompatibility, accused No.1 started residing separately,
and their marriage was mutually dissolved in M.C.No.1269/2006.

As per the settlement terms, the defacto complainant and accused No.1 were required to execute a registered partition/settlement deed to partition their respective 50% undivided share in the property within two days from the filing of the joint memo, and withdraw the criminal cases filed against the defacto complainant.
3. Accused Nos.1 with the intention to cheat, executed a Power Of Attorney in favor of Accused No.2.

Subsequently, on the basis of power of attorney,accused No.2 got accused No.1's name NC:
2024:KHC:10673 entered into the Khata maintained by Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the name of accused No.1 was entered into the Khatha maintained by the Bruhath Bangalore Mahanagara Palike to the extent of 50% in the subject site pursuant to a registered partition deed, which was executed following the order passed by the I Additional Principal Family Judge, Bangalore City, in execution No.90/2013.

5. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 contends that accused No.1, while suppressing her second marriage, induced the defacto complainant to enter into a settlement before the family court and fraudulently obtained the registered partition deed.

sentences.text: The veracity of the allegations against the petitioners can only be considered at the time of trial and cannot be examined in this petition.
6. The learned High Court Government Pleader reiterates the submission made by the learned counsel for respondent No.1.

Having considered the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties and perused the record, The respondent No.1 had filed Miscellaneous No.198/2018 before the I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore, seeking to recall the compromise decree dated 09.09.2008 passed in M.C.No.1269/2006.

entities.text: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It was NC: 2024:KHC:10673 alleged that the compromise decree was obtained fraudulently by suppressing the fact that accused No.1 had contracted a second marriage during the subsistence of the first marriage.

The family court, by its order dated 12.09.2022, dismissed the petition, stating that the second marriage was contracted after the compromise decree.
7.

The family court's finding that the second marriage was contracted after the compromise decree was drawn renders the allegation that accused No.1 suppressed her second marriage to induce the defacto complainant into a compromise without substance.

Subsequent to the registered partition deed, the accused No.1 executed a special power of attorney in favor of accused No.2, the basis on which the name of the accused No.1 was entered in property records of BBMP, which cannot be said to be fraudulent or has resulted in cheating the defacto complainant.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.18845/2018 on the file of IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore stands quashed.
